unresolved_source_conventions.detail: Sufficient regularity and an appropriate prior are not fully quantified in Theorem 2 itself. The source explicitly points to Theorems 9 and 10; their detailed setting and the posterior-mean paragraph are archived. No claim is made for arbitrary Gaussian priors or for the optional algebraic rate absent its condition.

Theorem 4 says in the setting of Theorem 3, but its supremum prints an Hs ball and positivity without the explicit C2 norm bound of Theorem 3. Both source clauses are retained; the census does not silently change the supremum to a norm-sum ball.

The infimum includes all measurable bounded-L2-operator-valued estimators, while the loss uses an H2-to-H2 operator norm. An arbitrary bounded L2 operator need not map H2 into H2. The source does not state an extended-infinity convention or restrict the estimator class further.

Theorem 7 refers to (12) for gamma. The adjoining text gives 1/3 under an interpolation invoking s>=2 and qualitative gamma(s) approaching one with smoothness. It gives no complete explicit formula for all s>d, particularly when d=1 and s<2. The reference and qualification are preserved.

The source asserts that Euclidean distance-neighborhood enlargements of the hyperrectangle have smooth boundaries for every m. Such offsets generally have joins between flat and curved pieces and need not have a C-infinity boundary. The displayed domain and the assertion are preserved separately from the general smooth-domain requirement; no alternative smoothing construction is invented.

The general diffusion setup normalizes volume to one, whereas the geometric construction retains width w>=2 and a positive enlargement. The explicit O_(m,w) is not volume one as written. The normalization is kept as an ambient convention with this scope discrepancy, rather than changing the geometric definition or automatically adding a unit-volume hypothesis to Theorem 8.

The source calls indices 0 through K the first K eigenfunctions, although there are K+1 including the constant mode. It also prints mixed strict and non-strict signs in the eigenvalue ordering. These are preserved without imposing simplicity. The estimator basis instead uses 0 through J-1.

The defining empirical matrix has zero coefficients outside both retained index ranges. The expected full-L2 operator is therefore a two-sided compression, while the next paragraph writes only pi_EJ P_D,f. The defining estimator is preserved and the discrepancy is separately documented.

KL is defined for arguments in F, introduced as a positive C2 class. Theorem 11 instead explicitly assumes Proposition 2B, whose opening condition is C1 with Hs bounds for s>d. Those bounds alone need not yield C2 for every allowed s,d. The source does not explain whether F additionally restricts this theorem; both clauses are retained without silently upgrading its stated regularity.

Page 5 defines integer-order Sobolev/Hölder spaces explicitly but the theorems allow real s; the fractional Sobolev convention is left standard rather than given an invented formula. The same paragraph calls the HS norm a norm on operators on a Banach space; the actual theorem applications use the Hilbert space L2. Page 17 ends a squared-dual-norm comparison with an unsquared L2 norm, retained only as source prose.

The logarithmic modulus contains reciprocal operator difference. At equality of the two operators the printed expression requires a limiting endpoint interpretation, consistent with the ensuing injectivity sentence; the source does not define that endpoint separately.

The posterior-mean paragraph writes the preceding polynomial tilde-delta_N rate without restating its spectral hypothesis. Theorem 10 distinguishes the baseline logarithmic rate from an optional polynomial rate, and Theorem 2 states only consistency. The proof shorthand is not promoted to an unconditional theorem conclusion.
